title: Archive or rewrite epic-19 sync stories 19-8/19-9 — both still target a SyncEngine/syncEngineProvider architecture that has been deleted
rule: Tier-4 triage protocol (presents-as-current vs point-in-time); related AG-8/AG-9

evidence.quote: SUPERSEDED-ARCHITECTURE NOTE: This story's activation rule ("has Firebase account → activate") is from the March model.
W2.35: [syncEngineProvider] deleted — this is the sole write-path provider.

why: These are the only two files in the batch still marked ready-for-dev, i.e. presented as live, pickable backlog rather than history. Both prescribe editing lib/features/sync/data/sync_engine.dart, making syncEngineProvider nullable, and adding SyncEngine.pushAllLocalData()/OfflineQueue.enqueue* calls. None of that exists anymore: SyncEngine, syncEngineProvider, and sync_engine.dart itself were deleted during the SyncOrchestrator+outbox rewrite (proven by the DNI-333/334/335 decomposition stories in this same batch and by the 'syncEngineProvider deleted' comment in sync_providers.dart) — the only remaining trace is a `.skip`-suffixed dead test file (test/features/sync/data/sync_engine_test.dart.skip). This repo runs an autonomous batch/worktree-per-story workflow (evidenced by the DNI-378..383 dev-agent records in this batch); a developer or agent that pulls '19-8' or '19-9' off the ready-for-dev backlog would burn a full worktree cycle trying to resurrect a provider that was deliberately deleted, risking a regression to the pre-outbox sync design. 19-8's own AC-3 goal (SyncStatus.localOnly) is already shipped via SyncOrchestrator, so the story is redundant as well as stale — only 19-8 carries a partial self-aware 'SUPERSEDED-ARCHITECTURE' note (and even that leaves Status at ready-for-dev); 19-9 carries no such warning at all.
recommendation: Move 19-8 and 19-9 to docs/_archive/superseded/ (the repo already uses this location, e.g. docs/_archive/superseded/epic-15-stories/15.11-profile-scoped-providers-sync.md) with a pointer to what actually replaced them (DNI-333/334/335 SyncEngine decomp, DNI-342 tier threading, the SyncOrchestrator/outbox architecture) — or rewrite their ACs against SyncOrchestrator if the underlying user-facing goal is still open. Add a cheap Rule-0 doc-lint: for every docs/stories/implementation/*.md with Status in {ready-for-dev, backlog, todo}, grep the class/provider names listed under its 'File:' targets against lib/ and fail the audit if a named symbol doesn't resolve — this would have caught the drift immediately.
acceptance_criteria: 19-8 and 19-9 no longer sit at Status: ready-for-dev while referencing symbols (SyncEngine, syncEngineProvider) absent from lib/ — either archived/superseded-tagged or rewritten against SyncOrchestrator.
A grep-based checker (make audit target or tool/ script) flags any ready-for-dev/backlog story whose 'File:' targets don't exist in lib/, preventing silent recurrence.

corrections: Minor: other epic-19 stories (19-2,19-3,19-4,19-6,19-10,19-11,19-12) also carry ready-for-dev status, so 'only two files' may be scoped to the source batch rather than all of epic-19 — doesn't invalidate the 19-8/19-9 claims themselves.
